analysis: This PR changes only docs/threat-model.yaml. The two primary units are base_text (lines 1-897). The base side has no changed ranges. Head changes add three blocks. First, a header note at head 43-45 saying TB-012, A-018 and T-059 describe the add-on hold socket, its signature check, leases and the machine-lock fallback, with coordinator busy-field handling left as separate platform work. Second, A-018 provider_serving_availability at head 232-241 (sensitivity medium), citing provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Addon/ProviderLoop+AddonHold.swift. Third, TB-012 provider_to_local_addon_hold_socket starting at head 811: a separately signed io.darkbloom.sandbox add-on asks the provider over an owner-only AF_UNIX socket to stop inference while VMs run, and both run as the same user. There is also a change at head 2305-2337, presumably T-059, which was not visible because the patch excerpt is truncated. The documented hold only withholds serving availability, A-018. Under TB-003 the operator (ADV-001) already controls the process and can stop serving, so a same-user hold adds no confidentiality or authorization capability over A-001, A-003, A-015 or A-016 as described. I found no concrete regression in the visible text. Questions for integration: (1) Does the T-059 text at head 2305-2337, and the rest of TB-012, accurately describe: what the signature check authenticates; whether other same-user processes can open the socket; lease expiry and fail-open versus fail-closed behavior if the add-on crashes; machine-lock stale handling? (2) Does a hold ever cause the provider to drop in-flight requests without the inference_error and fail-closed encryption behavior required by T-008 and T-010, or skip final-handoff checks? (3) Coordinator busy-field routing is platform-owned; confirm the busy fields are not treated as trust evidence (T-052). (4) The provider-swift add-on source was not supplied. That is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety.
